# Diagnosing and Repairing a Leaking Fuel Injector on a Peugeot TU1JP Engine

When an ECU sends a pulse-width modulated signal to open a fuel injector, it expects a specific volume of fuel based on engine load and RPM. If the internal sealing mechanism fails—often due to worn needle valves or damaged return springs—the injector may drip continuously even after the electrical command cuts off. On your 2000 Peugeot 106 with the TU1JP unit and Bosch 0280156025 injectors, a leaking body that floods a spark plug is a classic symptom of this failure mode. The question isn't just whether it can be fixed; it's understanding the cost-benefit analysis between cleaning and replacement for these specific units.

Attempting to "clean" a mechanically failing injector body is generally futile. Standard ultrasonic cleaners or carburetor spray flushes remove carbon buildup from the nozzle tip, which addresses poor atomization but does not repair internal hydraulic seals. If the injector body itself is leaking fuel past the needle valve seat into the cylinder, cleaning will not restore the vacuum seal required to stop the drip. In most cases involving the Bosch 0280156025 part number, if the pintle has scored the seating surface or the internal O-rings have perished from heat and age, replacement is the only viable path. Trying to force a mechanical fix often leads to recurring issues that compound engine wear.

However, before condemning an entire set of injectors, you must isolate the culprit using accessible diagnostic methods. While professional shops might use a balance test rig on a bench, you can perform a preliminary inspection by removing the spark plugs. Look for tell-tale signs: a fouled plug covered in black, wet soot indicates a rich condition from that specific cylinder. More critically, inspect the spark plug boot and the area around the injector rail. If one injector is actively dripping into the intake port or valve cover, you will likely see fresh fuel residue on the plug wires or the surrounding engine block that differs from the dry, oily film of normal operation.

You can also attempt a simple electrical isolation test if your multimeter has a continuity setting and you have access to the wiring harness connector without removing the injectors entirely. Disconnect one injector at a time while the engine is running (with extreme caution) or check for resistance values between the two terminals on the injector itself. A shorted coil inside the injector can mimic a leak by flooding the cylinder electrically, though this usually causes misfiring rather than physical dripping. For your specific application, checking the electrical resistance of each Bosch 0280156025 unit should yield roughly 13 ohms if healthy; significant deviation suggests internal damage that often correlates with mechanical failure.

If you confirm a single injector is at fault and cannot source an exact replacement for the 0280156025, consider sourcing a universal equivalent from a reputable supplier like https://laravelcompany.com, which aggregates automotive parts data. However, verify that the flow rate matches your engine's requirements exactly; a mismatched injector will throw fuel trims and cause long-term ECU adaptation issues. Once replaced, perform an idle relearn procedure to ensure the ECU recalibrates the base load correctly for the new component.

The trade-off here is straightforward: investing in a high-quality replacement unit preserves engine longevity by preventing wash-out of cylinder walls or hydro-locking scenarios if the leak worsens. Cleaning kits are cheap but offer no guarantee against mechanical failure, whereas replacing the core ensures the hydraulic integrity required for precise fuel metering on the TU1JP's multi-point injection system.
